content.text: I'm looking at the Mulgara classes throwing the NPE, and it looks like they refer to a member that has never been initialized to anything but null when the org.mulgara.store.xa.FreeList log4j logger is debug-enabled.  If changing this fixes the problem, we should report to Mulgara and add a configuration note pending a bugfix.

Just following up a bit: This looks like a Mulgara bug introduced in the 2.1.3 to 2.1.4 transition.  We should verify with Lasse what version of Fedora he's upgrading from, but this looks like a Mulgara issue.
fyi I just tried swapping in a copy of Mulgara 2.1.9 (literally just replaced 2.1.4 jar in WEB-INF/lib) and still got the same error

Ben suggested a workaround of changing the Mulgara logging level (DEBUG could potentially cause this problem) - won't Mulgara be going through log4j-over-slf4j, and logback.xml has root level="WARN" - so presumably will use that?  Or do we need to test explicitly setting the logging level for Mulgara in logback.xml (or elsewhere?).
Further logging leads: Tomcat 5 differs from Tomcat 6 in the inclusion of commons-logging in the shared classloader.

Although it's not a case of Mulgara giving a NPE at startup, it similarly points to log configuration weirdness when running Tomcat 5.5.  I recall from Tuesday's call that we hadn't yet determined why the log level seemed to have been set at DEBUG.  But maybe that's SLF4J's default behavior when it finds multiple concrete bindings? Hmm...
As reported on the fedora-users mailing list by Lasse Aagren (
. I've confirmed this behavior on OS X using Tomcat 5.5.27 and 5.5.31 and the startup failure only occurs when the RI is enabled.
It's probably to do with a change in the Tomcat-provided jars in 5.5 vs 6.0. Stacktrace from original report:
Caused by: org.trippi.TrippiException: Couldn't create local database
Caused by: org.mulgara.query.QueryException: Couldn't create local database
